title: Apple Music Introduces AI Labels for Tracks, Following Spotify and Industry Push
excerpt: New Transparency Tags flag AI-generated content across music, artwork, and videos, but enforcement relies entirely on labels and distributors to opt in.
body:
• Apple Music has introduced "Transparency Tags" that flag when AI was used to create a track, composition, artwork, or music video.
  • The system is voluntary: labels and distributors decide whether to apply tags, with no enforcement mechanism from Apple.
  • The move follows Spotify's September 2025 AI-disclosure labels and a broader RIAA-led push for industry-wide AI labeling on streaming platforms.
  • Deezer, which receives over 60,000 fully AI-generated tracks daily, has taken a stricter approach with automated in-house AI detection.

Apple Music has rolled out a labeling system for AI-generated content, joining Spotify and Deezer in an industry-wide effort to let listeners know when artificial intelligence had a hand in making the music they hear.

The company's new "Transparency Tags," detailed in a newsletter to industry partners first reported by Music Business Worldwide, cover four categories: tracks, compositions, artwork, and music videos. Any content created "in whole or in part" by AI can now carry a tag — if the label or distributor chooses to apply one.

Voluntary by Design

Apple is leaving the decision squarely with content providers. "Proper tagging of content is the first step in giving the music industry the data and tools needed to develop thoughtful policies around AI, and we believe labels and distributors must take an active role in reporting when the content they deliver is created using AI," the company wrote.

The tags can be used immediately and "will be required when delivering new content to Apple Music in the future," according to Music Ally, which also obtained the newsletter. But Apple has no apparent enforcement mechanism — no automated detection, no penalties for non-disclosure.

"Similar to genres, credits, and other metadata, Apple defers to content providers to determine what qualifies as AI content."

— Apple, in its newsletter to industry partners

An Industry-Wide Push

Apple's move arrives amid a broader campaign led by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) and the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI). The coalition, which includes the Recording Academy, SAG-AFTRA, and the American Association of Independent Music, is pushing streaming platforms to adopt standardized AI labels.

The proposed system would use two labels: a black tile with "AI" in white capitals for fully AI-generated tracks, and a white tile with lowercase "ai" for songs where humans used AI as a creative tool. The labels would function much like the existing explicit-content warning, according to the Wall Street Journal, which first reported the initiative in July 2026.

Spotify had already moved in this direction, announcing AI-disclosure labels in September 2025 alongside a policy that enables removal of AI voice impersonations made without an artist's consent. Apple's Transparency Tags follow a similar opt-in model.

The Scale of the Problem

The urgency behind labeling is clearest in the numbers. Deezer, the French streaming platform, disclosed in January 2026 that it receives more than 60,000 fully AI-generated tracks every day — double the number it saw in September 2025. The platform has identified 13.4 million AI-generated tracks in its catalog.

A Deezer-commissioned Ipsos study found that 97 percent of listeners could not distinguish AI-generated songs from human-made ones. Yet 80 percent said they wanted fully AI-generated tracks clearly labeled.

Unlike Apple and Spotify, Deezer has deployed in-house AI-detection tools that flag content regardless of whether the distributor opts in.

What Comes Next

For now, the initiative covers audio tracks only. The RIAA-led coalition has not proposed labels for AI-generated lyrics, album artwork, or music videos. Whether Apple extends its tags beyond the current voluntary framework — or adds detection technology — remains to be seen.

The debate has clear relevance for India's rapidly growing music streaming market, where platforms like JioSaavn, Gaana, and Spotify India are competing for listeners in a market projected to cross 600 million users by 2028. As AI-generated content floods global catalogs, Indian labels and independent artists face the same transparency challenge now playing out in the West.
